abstract: Multimodal language models continue to improve on broad music understanding benchmarks, but which musical features can they perceive and reason about? We investigate this question by introducing PianoBench, a benchmark that tasks language models with reasoning about musical performances across congruent acoustic and symbolic input representations. PianoBench is derived from our new multimodal, training-scale dataset comprising more than 20,000 hours of interleaved transcripts of music and spoken musical commentary from instructional piano videos. Open-weight audio-language models achieve at most 52.8% accuracy on PianoBench, and at best only modestly outperform their accuracy on a no-audio control. In contrast, frontier models using chain of thought achieve up to 93.2% accuracy when provided transcripts of music as text, exposing a gap between perceiving musical features from audio and reasoning about musical events when they are given explicitly. We then test whether mid-training on interleaved musical instruction can improve question answering without chain of thought, raising Qwen 3.5 9B Base's zero-shot accuracy on PianoBench with music transcripts from 42.8% to 56.0% after instruction tuning. These experiments suggest that instructional videos may represent an overlooked source of multimodal supervision for music. Available: https://gclef-cmu.org/pianobench.

oneSentenceThesis: PianoBench 用同一钢琴片段的音频和乐谱文本两种输入考查模型，发现开源音频模型几乎不能从声音中提取答题线索，而前沿模型在给定显式音符加思维链时可达 93.2%，交错排列的教学讲解与演奏记录则能把 Qwen 3.5 9B 无思维链的文本推理从 42.8% 提升到 56.0%。
originalTitle: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models
readerTitle: 听得见和看得懂之间：PianoBench 如何区分音乐感知与推理
